reason: Same software (Zen Browser) across sources with genuinely different naming — Flathub's short display name "Zen" vs AUR's "zen-browser" family — that no safe name pattern can bridge on its own; zen alone is also now GENERIC_NAME_BLOCKLIST-ed (see group.ts) since it collides with an unrelated AUR C-language tool. User-reported false-negative merge.

Same software (GNOME Boxes) across sources with genuinely different naming — Flathub's short display name "Boxes" doesn't normalize-match "gnome-boxes", the name every native distro package (and Snap) uses instead. Found investigating the compat-warnings feature: "boxes" alone is also now GENERIC_NAME_BLOCKLIST-ed (see group.ts) since it was wrongly false-merging with an unrelated ASCII-art text tool of the same name.

Same software (LibreOffice) — Arch's own release-channel naming (libreoffice-fresh, and its maintenance-branch twin libreoffice-still) never exact-matches any other source's bare "libreoffice" appId/name, so both stay stray standalone entries despite being kept (see filter-keep.json). Found during an ultra-style review pass that also uncovered the keep-list coverage gap for LibreOffice/LibreCAD across apk-alpine/ebuild-gentoo/eopkg-solus/nix-nixpkgs/snap-snapcraft/xbps-void.

Same software (Beeper) as the new official beeper.com AppImage entry — AUR's beeper-bin/beeper-nightly-bin already auto-merge with it via tier2's normalized-name match (both normalize to "beeper"), but beeper-v4-bin's "v4" isn't a recognized AUR channel-word/variant-suffix component (see group.ts's AUR_CHANNEL_WORD/AUR_VARIANT_SUFFIX), so it strips down to "beeper-v4" instead and stays a stray. User-reported — needed for baxyz's influencer recommendations page.

Same software (Node.js) — Snap's official "Node.js Runtime" snap is named "node", not "nodejs" like every other source's bare-appId package (Alpine/Arch/Debian/Ubuntu/Gentoo/Nixpkgs/Slackware/Solus/Void, already unioned into one group via tier1's exact appId match), so it stays a stray standalone entry. User-reported. Fedora's nodejs20/22/24/26 deliberately NOT included here — real, separately-installable parallel major-version-stream packages (Fedora Modularity convention, no single unversioned "nodejs" package exists there), not duplicate names for the same install target.
